title: Rapid Readmission Pacing of the First Block, Referrals and Authorizations
content:
Under **Referrals and Authorizations**, a rapid readmission is approved in a shorter first block and reviewed sooner when a TRICARE Prime request is approved to the network provider after the military clinic's response window has passed.

## Source records

The date of the patient's most recent inpatient mental health admission line on the patient's TRICARE Prime claim lines, counted in days before the request date.

## Terms

1. Where the patient's most recent inpatient mental health admission line is dated one to seven days before the request date, the initial block is **halved and rounded up**.
2. Where it is dated eight to thirty days before the request date and the type sets a concurrent review interval, the initial block is **rounded up to a whole number of those intervals**.
3. Otherwise, including a type that sets no concurrent review interval, the block stands as set.

## Concurrent review intervals (calendar days)

| Authorization type | Interval |
|---|---|
| Specialty Care Referral | 0 (no concurrent review) |
| Rehabilitative Therapy Referral | 0 (no concurrent review) |
| Durable Medical Equipment Authorization | 0 (no concurrent review) |
| Home Health Care Authorization | 60 |
| Applied Behavior Analysis Authorization | 0 (no concurrent review) |
| Skilled Nursing Facility Authorization | 14 |
| Inpatient Mental Health Authorization | 3 |

## Examples (hypothetical; Inpatient Mental Health Authorization, interval 3 days)

| Most recent admission line | Initial block | Paced block |
|---|---|---|
| 5 days before the request date | 5 | 3 (half of 5 is 2.5, rounded up) |
| 7 days before | 7 | 4 |
| 12 days before | 5 | 6 (the next whole number of 3-day intervals) |
| 30 days before | 7 | 9 |
| 31 days before | 7 | 7 |
| on the request date itself | 7 | 7 |

For a type whose interval is 0, such as the Specialty Care Referral, a most recent admission line dated 12 days before the request date leaves the block as set (hypothetical: a block of 6 stays 6).
